$comment: The upstream review ledger - version2.md section 7.1.
Every entry is a version somebody CHOSE. 'pinned' is what this project uses today;
'reviewed.upstream' is what upstream was serving the last time a person looked, and it is
the only field the detector compares against. When a live probe answers something else, that
entry has MOVED and owes a decision before the next release: re-pin it deliberately, or
upgrade it and validate against the suite.
Nothing here fails a build. 'dotnet run --project tools/FrameLink.Upstream -- check' is the
detector, and no build, test or publish invokes it. The only always-on check is the offline
test that keeps this file agreeing with the pins in source, which fails when a human changed
one and forgot the other - never because upstream published something overnight.
Debian package versions are deliberately NOT in scope. The apt resources move forward on
their own through security updates, by design, and the Fleet Manager records the versions it
finds. Recorded inventory is not a chosen version: an entry per Debian package would turn a
release gate into a daily chore, and a ceremony nobody performs is worse than none.

entries.title: Raspberry Pi OS Lite (Trixie, arm64) - the base image the section 3.9 generator writes into

reviewed.note: Measured against the file the URL served on 2026-08-15: the published .sha256 sidecar matched, the archive decompressed to the recorded length, and the image digest, the partition table and the three target directories were read back out of the result. Upstream publishes each image under a directory dated a day after the image itself - raspios_lite_arm64-2026-06-19 holds the 2026-06-18 image - so the probe's answer and the pin differ by that day and always will.

entries.title: Immich Kiosk - the slideshow the agent fetches and supervises (section 2.1, decision 41)

reviewed.note: Re-probed live on 2026-08-15 while the kiosk.binary.pinned-release resource was written, so this entry now points at the pin in source rather than at a paragraph. The release API answers v0.42.0 (published 2026-08-04); immich-kiosk_0.42.0_checksums.txt names 93476535e86dd6914b1b8e644fdc147b4770903434f0db15d0ee469e0857e423 for immich-kiosk_Linux_arm64.tar.gz and the 7,712,323 downloaded bytes hash to it; the archive holds LICENSE, README.md and one 18,546,850-byte immich-kiosk at 0755 whose Go build record reads -X main.version=0.42.0 with GOOS=linux GOARCH=arm64 CGO_ENABLED=0. KioskReleasePin carries both digests because they answer different questions: the published one gates the download, the binary one is what the resource observes on the frame every pass. One thing upstream does not offer is a bind address - main.go starts the server on ':' plus the port and the config struct has no host field - so the loopback-only property v1 had was Docker's port publishing, not Kiosk's, and kiosk.listen-address records the real bind set rather than claiming it. v1's compose file still names 0.39.3 and is not a consumer of anything v2 builds.

entries.title: Microsoft.Data.Sqlite - the Fleet Manager's store, EF Core being unusable under AOT (section 6.2)

reviewed.note: Floats by section 7.1: the reference is Version="*", and restore resolved 10.0.11 on 2026-08-15, which is what nuget.org served that day. A float cannot be held back without becoming a pin, so this entry moves the moment nuget.org does - which is the whole point of watching it, because the next build takes the new one whether or not anyone looked.

entries.title: xunit.v3 - the suite runner both the harness and the operator invoke

reviewed.note: Floats by section 7.1, resolved 4.0.0 on 2026-08-15. Worth a human's attention on every move rather than a shrug: 4.0.0 is the version whose dropped VSTest bridge is why the suite runs by executing the project directly instead of through dotnet test, and a runner change lands underneath every other gate in this repository.

entries.title: .NET LTS band - the target framework both programs are built against

reviewed.note: What is chosen here is the band, not the patch: net10.0 is LTS, in active support, EOL 2028-11-14, and .NET 8 and 9 were both out of support from 2026-11-10 (section 6.2). The probe answers with the channel's newest SDK, 10.0.400 on 2026-08-15; the workstation that built this ran 10.0.302 (section 6.1), which is a build-host fact rather than an artifact one, since Native AOT leaves no runtime for the frame to have. A support phase that stops being 'active' is the signal this entry exists to deliver.
